text:
maria: FYI I'm putting up a short benchmark plan to compare streaming vs non-streaming under the replay harness + synthetic Poisson generator. goal: isolate kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache warm/cold. suggestions?

rick: sounds good. propose a 3x2 matrix: (streaming, non-streaming, streaming-small-chunk) x (kv-warm, kv-cold). keep same trace for apples-to-apples latency distribution. also log kernel choices per request.

sanjay: add a control where we force kernel=A vs kernel=B (e.g., fused-attn vs baseline) so we can attribute regressions. also capture batch sizes over time.

elena: add a tiny end-to-end flow that uses tool-calling/structured-output so we exercise the streaming tokenizer path. otherwise streaming tests miss some codepaths.

yuki: perf-bot ran a quick sweep on a staging machine last night. summary: streaming with 4KB chunks + kv-cold shows a p99 delta +12% after the kernel selector change in main. we should bisect.

perf-bot: DEPLOY: test-run 2026-03-17T02:12Z, image: runtime-canary@sha256:abc123, config: max_batch=64,max_wait_ms=8,chunk_size=4096

maria: thanks. let's make the harness reproducible: seed the replay harness (trace offset + random jitter seed) and record the exact trace file. also pin model weights + quantization flags in metadata.

rick: agreed. here's the command I'm going to use for synthetic load:
```
./harness/generator --mode=replay --trace=traces/2026-03-prod-sampled.json --seed=42 --arrival=poisson --lambda=12 --clients=60 --streaming=true --chunk=4096
```
keep the same command but swap --streaming=false and chunk params for non-streaming.

sanjay: observation from earlier runs: client read loop + backpressure is the common root cause of spikes. if the client can't pull from socket fast enough with 4KB chunks we see bursts that block the runtime's readloop, resulting in larger batches and higher tail. try smaller chunk_size (512) as an experiment.

elena: note: for non-streaming we should still measure incremental kernel switch overhead because the runtime sometimes switches kernels mid-request for longer sequences. add trace markers when kernel switch happens.

yuki: added instrumentation PR: runtime logs `kernel_select=KX` and `kv_hit=true/false` per request now. also emits `batch_len` and `kernel_switch_count`.

maria: for metrics let's capture p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, tokens-per-second-per-gpu, batch_size histogram, and a time-series of kv_hit_rate and kernel distribution. have perf scripts dump JSON to s3 per run.

perf-bot: QUICKRESULT: 2026-03-17 02:45Z, streaming(4k)/kv-cold/kernelB -> p99 328ms (+12% vs baseline), avg batch_size 28, kernelB used 74% of requests, kv_hit_rate 12%

rick: that aligns with what I feared. kernelB probably has worse tight-loop for KV cold. next step: run a tight microbench comparing kernel B kv-lookup path with kernel A. record perf counters (L1/L2 misses, cycles).

sanjay: I ran perf on a micro-run: kernelB shows +35% cache-misses per token on kv lookup vs kernelA. snippet:
```
# perf stat -e cache-misses,cycles -r 5 ./bin/infer --profile-kv --seq-len=1024
cache-misses: 1,230,456
cycles: 45,234,000
```

elena: do we know if batching heuristics are amplifying the issue? i.e., kernelB + large batch_size = more memory pressure => more cache evictions => worse p99.

yuki: yes, when batch_size > 32 the cache-miss curve jumps. I'll add an experiment sweeping max_batch from 8,16,32,64 under kv-cold.

maria: good. also instrument client-side windows: how many in-flight chunks per connection. backpressure occurs when server-side queue grows while client still holding TCP window. try limiting clients*chunks-in-flight to reduce head-of-line stalls.

perf-bot: NOTE: observed client readloop stalls at kernel-switch boundaries. stack trace attached to run meta (s3://redwood-perf/runs/1790123456/trace.log).

rick: can someone pull a small flamegraph? if kernel switch triggers JIT/compilation or new kernel init, we'd see spikes. also check if kernel selection has locking around kernel table.

sanjay: i generated a flamegraph for the worst p99 sample. main takeaways: 40% time in `kv_lookup`, 18% in `kernel_switch_sync`, 12% in `client_read_loop`.

elena: action items: 1) Bisect kernel selector change to find offending commit. 2) Run batch sweep to find safe max_batch that avoids cache amplification. 3) Add client readloop backpressure telemetry (window size, in-flight chunks). 4) Add small-chunk streaming variant (512) in baseline matrix.

yuki: I'll open a perf ticket with attached CSVs and the harness commands + run artifacts. tagging @maria @rick.

maria: thanks — once yuki posts the ticket we'll schedule a 30m sync to decide whether we revert kernel selector or apply a heuristic: prefer kernelA for kv-cold or prefer smaller batches until cache warms.

deploy-bot: DEPLOYMENT: canary rolled back to runtime-canary@sha256:abc122 at 2026-03-17T03:05Z after metric alert (p99 > 300ms).

maria: perfect. let's keep the ticket focused on reproducible steps. if anyone runs other permutations, paste the exact harness command line and the s3 run path.

yuki: will do. thanks all! :thumbsup:
